articles.title: Georgia voters set early-voting record as midterm elections heat up
articles.summary: Brad Raffensperger praised record Georgia early voting turnout as the fiery Jon Ossoff and Mike Collins Senate debate exploded over personal attacks.
articles.body: Over 180,000 Georgians cast their ballots on the first day of early voting on Tuesday, setting a record for midterm elections. Tuesday's total eclipsed the first day of early voting in 2022 by more than 55,000 votes, state election officials say. Georgia's early voting schedule runs through Oct. 30. "This record-breaking turnout proves that voters have confidence in the integrity of our elections," Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger said in a statement. "It’s a testament to our strong election system overseen by 159 of the best county election officials in the country." Georgia's contentious U.S. Senate race erupted into a heated confrontation Tuesday night as Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., accused GOP challenger Rep. Mike Collins, R-Ga., of allowing the dissemination of "neo-Nazi propaganda" inside his own home, prompting Collins to fire back over Ossoff's financial support from a billionaire with ties to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. MAP IT: DOJ ILLEGAL VOTING CRACKDOWN SWEEPS 17 STATES AS RAZOR-THIN ELECTIONS FACE SCRUTINY The exchange unfolded during the candidates' second and final debate ahead of the Nov. 3 general election, which was hosted by the Atlanta Press Club and broadcast by Georgia Public Broadcasting network. ANTISEMITISM FIGHT EXPLODES IN FLORIDA AS VOTERS HEAD TO THE POLLS: 'POLITICAL POGROM' During the debate, Ossoff sought to tie his GOP opponent to White nationalism and repeatedly demanded that Collins commit to stopping the dissemination of hateful rhetoric involving his campaign staff, in particular Collins' son-in-law, which Ossoff alleged had continued despite blowback. "How weak a person do you have to be to be unable to stop someone under your own roof from disseminating neo-Nazi propaganda while you run for the Senate?" Ossoff asked, referencing reporting about his opponent's son-in-law, David Alan Scheer II, who was the subject of a CNN investigation about sharing Nazi propaganda imagery, promoting antisemitic conspiracy theories and polling his online followers about whether he should produce a video titled, "Why Gen-Z Doesn't Hate Hitler." FORMER HOUSE INTEL LEADER POINTS TO DEM RHETORIC 'ENCOURAGING' VIOLENCE; EIGHTH MAN CHARGED IN UFC TERROR PLOT Meanwhile, Collins accused his Democrat opponent of fueling threats against his family and refusing to return campaign support connected to LinkedIn co-founder Reid Hoffman, He also questioned Ossoff over his support for candidates linked to controversial streamer Hasan Piker. ‘MISLEADING VOTERS’: OSSOFF WARNS DONORS HE’S FALLING BEHIND DESPITE LEADING SENATE FUNDRAISING "I'm a little tired of this, Jon," Collins said. "There's a crazy person in jail right now because of your rhetoric," he alleged, before saying he had received another threat just the previous day. "Why don't you denounce that? Why don't you return that money?" Fox News' Alec Schemmel contributed to this report.

articles.title: Donald Trump estudia usar la MOAB, madre de todas las bombas, contra Irán: 10.000 kilos y poder explosivo de once toneladas de TNT
articles.standfirst: Estados Unidos contempla atacar de forma contundente su infraestructura energética
articles.summary: Estados Unidos contempla atacar de forma contundente su infraestructura energética
articles.body: El conflicto entre Estados Unidos e Irán no cesa. El ejército estadounidense no descarta, según fuentes consultadas por la CNN, utilizar la denominada MOAB para atacar su infraestructura energética y nuclear. Las siglas MOAB responden a Massive Ordnance Air Blast y es conocida popularmente como la madre de todas las bombas. Estos planes de ataque, de concretarse, supondrían un punto de inflexión en el conflicto entre Estados Unidos e Irán, según analiza la CNN. El citado medio mantiene que Donald Trump está siendo presionado para finalizar el conflicto y sus asesores califican el uso de la MOAB como un paso "definitivo". Todo apunta, de todos modos, a que desde la Casa Blanca no realizarán cambios bruscos de rumbo hasta que se celebren las elecciones de medio mandato (mid-term election), el próximo 3 de noviembre. La CNN, tras hablar con varios funcionarios conocedores de la situación, señala que algunos de ellos no consideran que usar la MOAB sea realmente eficaz para acabar con la infraestructura nuclear de Irán. Pese a su gran poder destructivo, no tendría, según estas fuentes, capacidad de penetración suficiente para acabar con determinadas instalaciones. Más allá de su eficacia desde el punto de vista militar, el citado medio plantea que el uso de este armamento podría servir a Estados Unidos para lanzar un mensaje simbólico a Irán. El último conflicto bélico entre ambos territorios se inició el pasado mes de febrero de este año. La MOAB, o GBU-43/B, es la bomba no atómica más potente del arsenal de Estados Unidos. Pesa 10.000 kilos, su diámetro de explosión es de 1,4 kilómetros y su poder destructivo equivale a once toneladas de TNT. El ejército estadounidense la utilizó por primera vez en un escenario bélico real en abril de 2017. Entonces, Donald Trump también era el inquilino de la Casa Blanca y la usó en Afganistán contra el Estado Islámico.
